name: assert_passkey
title: Sign in with a passkey
description: Sign a WebAuthn sign-in, as an authenticator does for navigator.credentials.get(): authenticator data and an ES256 signature over it and the client data's hash, with the vault's passkey for the site, plus the credential id and user handle a browser returns. With allow_credentials, only a passkey those ids name; without (a discoverable request), any discoverable passkey for the RP ID. When several can answer, the call is refused as several with the candidates: call again with credential_id. No passkey for the site is refused as no_credential. Hand the result only to the page that asked; the key never leaves this server.

rp_id.description: The RP ID: the site's domain the passkey is bound to, e.g. example.com or login.example.com.

client_data_hash.description: SHA-256 of the client data JSON the browser (or the program in its place) built for this request, base64url (43 characters).

items.description: A credential id, base64url as WebAuthn's JSON carries it.

allow_credentials.description: The request's allowCredentials ids; empty for a discoverable request.

credential_id.description: The passkey to sign with, from an earlier answer's candidates or list_passkeys.

user_verified.description: Whether the user was verified for this request, which sets the UV flag. True only when the caller verified them: an agent signing in as its own identity, or a person who approved the request.

name: check_exposed
title: Check a password against breaches
description: Whether a login's password appears in Have I Been Pwned's list of passwords seen in data breaches, and how many times. Only the first five hex characters of the password's SHA-1 leave this server (k-anonymity); the password and its full hash never do, and the answer is a count. A count above 0 means the password is known to attackers: rotate it (update_login with rotate_password, then change it on the site). With previous, the password the current one replaced.

previous.description: Check the password before the current one instead.

count.description: How many times the password was seen in breaches; 0 when it was not

name: create_login
title: Create login
description: Save a new login. Without `password` or `password_file` a strong one is generated here and stored; nothing returns it, so call get_password when you type it into the signup form. Create the login BEFORE submitting a signup, so the password is never lost. Filed into the collection Agents unless `collection` names another.

url.description: The site's URL, e.g. https://github.com/login; its host is what find_logins' url matches.

username.description: The login name or email the site knows the account by.

password.description: A password the account already has, exactly as you were given it. Leave it out to have a strong one generated here; a secret that is already in a file goes as password_file instead, so it is never retyped.

path.description: A path: a file in /srv/bitwarden-inbox (copy it there with cp; a bare name is taken from /srv/bitwarden-inbox). Links are refused.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

password_file.description: A password the account already has, from a file holding just it (one line; a final line ending is dropped): a downloaded key or a generated credential, which is safer read than retyped. Delete the file once the login is saved. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Copy the file into /srv/bitwarden-inbox and give its path, or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

length.description: Length of a generated password. Default 24.

symbols.description: Whether a generated password contains symbols (!@#$%^&*-_=+). Default true; turn off for sites that refuse them.

notes.description: Free text kept with the login: recovery codes, security answers, what the account is for.

totp_secret.description: The site's authenticator key: the base32 secret shown under the 2FA QR code, or the otpauth://totp/ URI it encodes. Store it BEFORE confirming 2FA on the site, then confirm with the code this call returns: the site accepting it proves the key was stored exactly.

collection.description: A collection name from health. Default: the collection Agents.

name: create_note
title: Create secure note
description: Save a secret that is not a login as a new secure note: a service account's key file, an API token, a licence key. Each secret goes in a field of its own, hidden by default, typed (value) or read from a file (file), with no password length limit: up to what Bitwarden stores in a field. Nothing returns the secret: the result names each field with its length, and a file's SHA-256 and size (compare them with the source's). get_field hands a value out; get_login names the fields. Filed into the collection Agents unless `collection` names another. If a call fails without saying whether the note was saved, find_logins by its name before trying again.

name.description: What the secret is, e.g. 'Play service account key (example-app)'.
The field's name, which get_field asks for, e.g. 'service account key (JSON)'. Names in one note must differ.

value.description: The value, typed exactly as you were given it. A secret that is already in a file goes as file instead, so it is never retyped.

file.description: The value from a file, taken whole and exactly: every line, a final line ending included (a JSON key file, a PEM key, a token). UTF-8 text up to 3695 bytes. Delete the file once the note is saved. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Copy the file into /srv/bitwarden-inbox and give its path, or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

path.description: A path: a file in /srv/bitwarden-inbox (copy it there with cp; a bare name is taken from /srv/bitwarden-inbox). Links are refused.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

hidden.description: A hidden field is a secret: get_login names it without its value. Default true; false for a plain detail such as a project id.

fields.description: The secrets, one field each, and any plain details beside them.

notes.description: Plain text anyone reading the note sees (get_login shows it): what the secret is for, where it is used. Never the secret itself.

collection.description: A collection name from health. Default: the collection Agents.

name: create_passkey
title: Create passkey
description: Register a new passkey, as an authenticator does for WebAuthn's navigator.credentials.create(): an ES256 (P-256) key pair is made here, the private key stored in the vault exactly as Bitwarden's own apps store a passkey (so they can sign with it too), and the answer is what a browser needs to finish the registration: the credential id, the attestation object (format none), the authenticator data and the public key (SPKI). The private key is never in the answer. It goes into the login item_id names, else into the one login already saved for this site with this username and no passkey, else into a new login named after the site (filed like create_login). Refused as excluded when the site's exclude list names a passkey the vault holds, and as unsupported when the site accepts no ES256 key. Use it for an agent's own identity; a person's own passkeys belong on their own devices.

rp_id.description: The RP ID: the site's domain the passkey is bound to, e.g. example.com or login.example.com.

rp_name.description: The site's name as the request gives it (rp.name).

id.description: The site's id for the account (user.id), base64url, 1 to 64 bytes.

name.description: The account's name at the site (user.name), usually its email or username.

client_data_hash.description: SHA-256 of the client data JSON for this request, base64url. An attestation of format none signs nothing, so it is only checked.

items.description: A credential id, base64url as WebAuthn's JSON carries it.

exclude_credentials.description: The request's excludeCredentials ids: passkeys the site already holds for this account.

algorithms.description: The COSE algorithm ids in the request's pubKeyCredParams, e.g. [-7, -257]. Empty means the default, which includes ES256 (-7).

resident_key.description: Whether the passkey is discoverable (a resident key), as the request's authenticatorSelection asks.

user_verified.description: Whether the user was verified for this request, which sets the UV flag. True only when the caller verified them: an agent signing in as its own identity, or a person who approved the request.

item_id.description: The login to put it in: one without a passkey, or whose passkey is for the same account on this site (it is replaced).

collection.description: For a new login: a collection name from health.

name: delete_passkey
title: Delete passkey
description: Remove one passkey from its login. The login and everything else in it (username, password, 2FA key) stay. The site keeps its copy of the public key, so remove the passkey there too if it should stop being offered. Not undone by anything here.

item_id.description: The login's item id, from list_passkeys or find_logins.

credential_id.description: The passkey's credential id, base64url, as list_passkeys gives it.

name: find_logins
title: Find logins
description: Search the vault's logins and secure notes (`kind` says which). `search` matches name, username and URL; `url` finds the logins saved for a site (its host, as Bitwarden's autofill matches). Returns ids, names, usernames and URLs, and whether each has a password and an authenticator key, never the secrets themselves. Syncs first, so an item just added in the web vault shows up.

search.description: Words in the name, username or URL.

url.description: The site's URL, e.g. https://github.com/login; its host is what find_logins' url matches.

limit.description: Return at most this many; `count` says how many matched.

name: get_field
title: Get field
description: One custom field's value, hidden ones included, from a login or a secure note: a secret that is not a password, such as a licence key or an API token, kept where a person put it. get_login names an item's fields. Use it only to type or pipe the value where it goes: never write it into a file, a commit, a message, a log or a reply.

field.description: The field's name as get_login lists it (case does not matter).

name: get_login
title: Get login
description: One login or secure note in full except its secrets: name, username, URLs, collections, notes, custom fields (hidden ones by name only) and when the password last changed.

name: get_password
title: Get password
description: The login's password, with its username and URLs, for typing into the site. Use it only for that: never write it into a file, a commit, a message, a log or a reply. With `previous`, the password the current one replaced, from the item's history: for when a site refused a rotation that is already stored.

previous.description: Return the password before the current one instead.

name: health
title: Health
description: Check that the vault is reachable and unlocked, and say as whom: the account, the server, when it last synced, how many logins and passkeys it holds, and the organizations and collections it can file into. Run this before concluding the MCP is broken.

name: import_passkeys
title: Import passkeys
description: Import the logins that carry passkeys from a Bitwarden JSON export (not encrypted), or from one exported item: each becomes a new login here with its username, password, 2FA key, URLs, notes, custom fields and passkeys, filed like create_login. A passkey the vault already holds is skipped, and so is one this server cannot sign with (only ES256 P-256 keys sign, as in Bitwarden's apps). The answer lists what was imported and what was skipped with the reason, and the file's SHA-256 and size: compare them with the source, then delete the file, which holds private keys.

path.description: A path: a file in /srv/bitwarden-inbox (copy it there with cp; a bare name is taken from /srv/bitwarden-inbox). Links are refused.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

filename.description: The file's name, for the answer.

file.description: The export. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Copy the file into /srv/bitwarden-inbox and give its path, or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

collection.description: A collection name from health, for every imported login. Default: as create_login.

name: list_passkeys
title: List passkeys
description: The passkeys the vault holds, each with its site (rpId and name), account (userName, userDisplayName, userHandle), credential id (base64url), counter, whether it is discoverable, when it was made, its login (itemId, itemName), the login's collections, and whether a person shared it with this account rather than the account keeping it as its own. Never a key. Syncs first.

rp_id.description: Only the passkeys for this RP ID, e.g. example.com.

search.description: Words in the site, its name, the account's names or the login's name.

limit.description: Return at most this many; `count` says how many matched.

name: move_item
title: Move item
description: Put a login or secure note in one collection: its collections become exactly the one named. Only between the collections of the item's own organization; an item in the account's own vault, or a collection of another organization, is refused with what to do instead. An item already in exactly that collection is left as it is (moved: false). After a move the vault is synced and the item read back, so the answer, its collections before and after, is what Bitwarden holds. Returns no secret. Nothing is deleted or copied.

collection.description: The collection to put it in: its name as health lists it (case does not matter), or its id.

collections.description: The item's collections now, by name

previousCollections.description: Its collections before the call, by name

moved.description: false when the item was already in exactly that collection, and nothing was sent

name: sync
title: Sync
description: Pull the vault from Bitwarden now. Reads already sync every 30 seconds; this is for right after someone changed something in the web vault.

name: totp
title: Current 2FA code
description: The login's current authenticator (TOTP) code and how many seconds it stays valid, computed from the key stored on the login. If fewer than 5 seconds are left, wait and call again.

name: update_login
title: Update login
description: Change a login: only what is named changes. `rotate_password` generates a new password and stores it at once; change it on the site right after, with get_password, and if the site refuses, get_password with previous: true still has the old one. `url` becomes the first URL and the others stay. `append_notes` adds to the notes (recovery codes, answers) where `notes` replaces them. Set `totp_secret` when you turn on 2FA at a site, before confirming it there: the result carries the current code from the stored key. A different key already on the login is replaced only with `replace_totp`, and kept in a hidden field.

url.description: The site's URL, e.g. https://github.com/login; its host is what find_logins' url matches.

username.description: The login name or email the site knows the account by.

password.description: A password the account already has, exactly as you were given it. Leave it out to have a strong one generated here; a secret that is already in a file goes as password_file instead, so it is never retyped.

path.description: A path: a file in /srv/bitwarden-inbox (copy it there with cp; a bare name is taken from /srv/bitwarden-inbox). Links are refused.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

password_file.description: A password the account already has, from a file holding just it (one line; a final line ending is dropped): a downloaded key or a generated credential, which is safer read than retyped. Delete the file once the login is saved. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Copy the file into /srv/bitwarden-inbox and give its path, or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

length.description: Length of a generated password. Default 24.

symbols.description: Whether a generated password contains symbols (!@#$%^&*-_=+). Default true; turn off for sites that refuse them.

append_notes.description: Added after the current notes on a new line; nothing is lost.

totp_secret.description: The site's authenticator key: the base32 secret shown under the 2FA QR code, or the otpauth://totp/ URI it encodes. Store it BEFORE confirming 2FA on the site, then confirm with the code this call returns: the site accepting it proves the key was stored exactly.

replace_totp.description: Replace a DIFFERENT authenticator key the login already has (or clear it with an empty totp_secret).
